world.bio: Priya Naidoo, 38, caseworker at a tenants' union in south Manchester. Spent nine years as an estate agent in Didsbury before I got sick of being the person who told families the rent was going up again. Now I sit on the other side of the desk: damp, disrepair, deposits, section 21 notices. I keep a spreadsheet of every landlord and managing agent that ever ignored a repair. 412 rows and counting. Come and say hello if your landlord is one of them.
skills_assets: Casebook of 380 closed and open cases since 2020, tagged by landlord, agent, ward and defect type
Knows the Housing Act 2004 HHSRS process, how Category 1 hazards get scored, and what the council's private-sector housing team will and won't act on
Her casebook notes that once the council's private-sector housing team serves an improvement notice, a retaliatory no-fault eviction is blocked for six months
Template letters for disrepair, deposit protection, and Tenant Fees Act breaches
Six years of contacts: two solicitors at a housing law firm, three environmental health officers, a local councillor on the housing committee
Damp meter, thermal camera borrowed from a community energy group, and a camera phone

projects.name: Levenshulme damp-and-mould case file
projects.text: She is assembling Levenshulme damp-and-mould cases for a meeting with the council's housing enforcement team next month. So far 23 households, 14 with photos and dated emails, eight with a medical letter linking mould to a child's asthma. The aim is to show the pattern across three landlords and one managing agent, rather than 23 separate complaints they can each shrug off. Need at least 30 well-documented cases before the meeting. Chasing the last seven.

projects.name: Landlord spreadsheet clean-up
projects.text: Cleaning up the 412-row landlord and agent sheet, merging duplicates (same landlord under four company names), and adding Companies House numbers. Want to publish an anonymised version as a 'worst agents' league table for the union newsletter. Legal says to be careful: every entry needs two corroborated cases.

projects.name: Portuguese on an app
projects.text: Trying to learn Portuguese before a trip to Lisbon in April with my sister. Day 41 of the streak. Can order a pastel de nata and complain about a boiler, which seems enough.

notes.text: Took the greyhound to training class at the park. Mabel is a rescue, three years old, terrified of bin lorries. Instructor says use treats and distance. We managed to walk past a skip without her bolting. Treat budget: roughly a whole chicken breast.

Case on Stockport Road: single mum, boiler dead since July, children sleeping in coats. Agent says contractor is 'booked'. I rang six times. Wrote the improvement notice request myself because the environmental health officer said they'd only visit if someone formally asked. Why does it take a formal ask to turn on someone's heating?
Allotment waiting list: I'm number 61 for the plot on Fog Lane. Told it will be 'about six years'. Ordered a tub of cress seeds for the windowsill instead. Mabel ate one.

The Levenshulme sheet. Another household called today. Damp in the back bedroom, black mould, the landlord painted over it. Photos of mould under fresh paint, bubbling. This is the sort of image that makes the case, much more than a paragraph.

Dreamt I was an estate agent again and had to show a flat with a hole in the ceiling. Told the viewer 'it's got character'. Woke up sweating. Therapy joke: the person with the best landlord spreadsheet in Manchester used to be the person writing the listings.

Rang a solicitor friend about retaliatory eviction. Reminded me of the rule: once the council has served an improvement notice, the landlord can't serve a section 21 for six months. It's the most useful sentence in my job and the one tenants never hear. Wrote it on a sticky note and stuck it above my monitor.
Team meeting. Union wants to run a 'know your rights' stall at the Levenshulme market. I volunteered, then remembered it's the weekend with the greyhound walking club. Double-booked myself. Typical.
Portuguese: my app's owl is furious. Missed two days. Spent the evening chasing a missing medical letter instead. Priorities.

Had a tenant in tears at the office today because a no-fault eviction notice arrived two weeks after she reported mould. She'd not asked us for help beforehand. I said we can still fight, but the clock is tight. Hate that the timing keeps being the cruelty.
Counted again: 27 cases ready for the Levenshulme file. Three short. Emailed the others. Mabel slept on my feet all evening.

messages.text:
Anita: Did you see the flight prices for April?
Me: Not yet. How bad?
Anita: Eighty quid cheaper if we book now.
Me: Book it. I'll pay you back Friday.

Dave: We got your request for Stockport Rd. Visiting Thursday.
Me: Thank you. Can the tenant be there?
Dave: Better if she is.
Me: She'll be there.

Marcus: Can you cover the Monday drop-in?
Me: What's on?
Marcus: Deposit disputes, mostly.
Me: Fine. Bring biscuits.

Jo: Mabel did brilliantly. Next session, we try the busy road.
Me: Brave.
Jo: Bring cheese.

Hannah: I can sit in for an hour on the enforcement team meeting if you want legal backup.
Me: Please. Would be great.
Hannah: Send me the case list first.

relations.about: Lives in Leeds, a primary school teacher, my travelling partner
Rescue greyhound, afraid of loud noises, loves lying on radiators
Colleague who handles benefits cases, shares my office

constraints: Won't take cases that need court representation without a solicitor
Can't see walk-ins outside the drop-in hours because of caseload
Working hours 9-5 four days a week
Won't name landlords publicly without two corroborated cases
sensitive: Burnt out in February, took two weeks off
Her own flat has a damp patch she hasn't reported because she doesn't want to fight her own landlord
